cards.claim: The default quota for DB instances is 40 per account in each Region (20 in ap-south-1), and the quota is adjustable.
cards.scope: per account, per Region; default; adjustable; ap-south-1 has a default of 20.

cards.claim: Amazon RDS (not counting Aurora) offers these database engines: IBM Db2, MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle Database, and PostgreSQL.
cards.scope: Amazon RDS user guide (engines other than Aurora).

cards.claim: Amazon RDS manages backups, software patching, automatic failure detection and recovery.
An RDS DB subnet group requires a subnet in at least two Availability Zones, which also makes it easy to switch to a Multi-AZ deployment later.
links: [a subnet in at least two Availability Zones](../facts/rds.md#rds-subnet-group-two-azs)

cards.claim: A DB subnet group should have at least one subnet in every Availability Zone of the Region.
links: [at least one subnet for every Availability Zone](../facts/rds.md#rds-faq-subnet-group-every-az)

cards.claim: A DB subnet group can hold at most 20 subnets, and this quota is not adjustable.
cards.scope: per DB subnet group; maximum; not adjustable.

cards.claim: A DB instance created without a DB parameter group uses a default one, and the settings of a default parameter group cannot be modified; to change parameters you create a custom parameter group and associate it with the instance.
If you create a DB instance without specifying a DB parameter group, a default DB parameter group is used.
cards.scope: per DB instance created without a DB parameter group; default; adjustable.

cards.claim: Updating parameters in a DB parameter group changes them for every DB instance associated with that group.
cards.scope: DB parameter groups and option groups.

cards.claim: For RDS for PostgreSQL, the rds.force_ssl parameter requires SSL connections; its default is 1 (on) for version 15 and later and 0 (off) for 14 and older, and changing it needs a custom DB parameter group.
cards.scope: RDS for PostgreSQL; default; adjustable; default depends on major version.

cards.claim: Applications can use SSL/TLS to encrypt connections to RDS databases running Db2, MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle or PostgreSQL, optionally verifying the server certificate.
cards.scope: encryption in transit (SSL/TLS) to RDS databases.

cards.claim: A pending-reboot parameter group status does not cause an automatic reboot in the next maintenance window; you must reboot the DB instance manually to apply the changes.
